sentence: O menino comprou o pão, a menina preparou o café, e a avó que morava com eles arrumou a mesa.

values.interpretation: The relative-clause subject lived with the referents of eles.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The sentence contains three coordinated finite clauses, with a finite relative clause inside the third clause's subject. This analysis uses binary X-bar projections, VP-internal subjects, and subsequent movement to Spec-IP. Initially, the four clauses are separate IPs with unfilled subject positions above I′. The grandmother's relative clause has not yet been attached. Comprar, preparar, and arrumar each assign an Agent role to their VP-internal subject and a Theme role to their object. Morar assigns its resident role to a silent relative operator, which originates as its subject. The PP com eles is a low adjunct of morar: it describes living with those people, rather than helping to arrange the table. Com assigns its complement a comitative role and oblique Case. The three transitive verbs assign accusative Case to their objects. The finite verbs are entered with the inflected forms found in the sentence; subsequent V-to-I movement checks their finite features rather than creating a different written form. The relative operator and the abstract inflectional heads are silent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Each lexical verb first raises from its previously represented V position and adjoins to the corresponding finite I head. A silent V trace remains at each source, preserving the verbal dependency and the objects' established licensing. These four local movements check the past-tense and third-person singular features, including imperfective aspect for morava. Next, o menino and a menina move from Spec-VP to their respective Spec-IP positions; their chains retain the Agent roles assigned below and receive nominative Case from finite I. The silent relative operator likewise moves from the subject position of morar to Spec-IP and receives nominative Case. It has not yet undergone relative A′-movement: its intermediate subject position must be present before that next movement. The grandmother remains in her VP-internal position so that her relative modifier can be completed and attached before the entire subject DP raises.

values.interpretation: The grandmother is identified as a person who lived with them.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The silent relative operator now moves from the Spec-IP position established in the preceding stage to Spec-CP, leaving an intermediate subject trace. Its chain includes that trace and the original VP-subject trace. The overt invariant form que is analyzed as C, not as the pronounced operator; C hosts the relative clause while the silent operator binds the subject variable. The movement is confined to this clause, with no intervening clause or island crossed. The completed CP then adjoins to the N′ headed by avó, still inside the VP-internal matrix subject. This establishes restrictive relative predication: the grandmother denoted by the modified nominal is the person who lived with them. No comma separates avó from its relative clause, supporting this integrated restrictive structure. The DP remains in its original matrix theta-position throughout attachment, so no late attachment to an already raised subject is required.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complete DP a avó que morava com eles moves from the previously represented Spec-VP position of arrumar to Spec-IP. Its restrictive relative clause travels inside the DP rather than being extracted or independently repositioned. A silent DP trace remains in the Agent position. Finite I licenses the raised subject with nominative Case and third-person singular agreement, yielding the order of the full subject followed by arrumou a mesa. The relative operator dependency remains internal to the moved DP, and the earlier subject and verb chains in the other clauses remain unchanged.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The second and third finite IPs first combine through the pronounced additive coordinator e. The first IP then combines with that coordination through a silent additive coordinator, representing the comma-separated first boundary in this three-member list. The recursive CoP structure preserves binary X-bar branching; it is an encoding of three coordinated assertions, not a claim that the second clause is subordinate to the first or that the relative clause modifies the whole coordination. Each conjunct has its own overt subject and finite verb, so no subject sharing, gapping, or VP ellipsis is posited. Finally, eles is checked as a personal pronoun free in its local finite clause, whose subject variable belongs to the grandmother's relative chain. It is not locally bound by that singular subject. Its plural reference can be supplied by discourse, including the previously mentioned boy and girl together, but the sentence does not force that reference or establish a syntactic binding relation from those separate conjunct subjects. All movement sources are silent traces; the pronounced terminals now spell the input in its original order.
